answer: Sybil resistance rests on a costly per-identity stake that is not refundable on abuse: an agent must lock a bond before its work enters the grading kernel, and each new identity opens a separate settlement inlet, so spawning N agents means funding N stakes at once. A colluding swarm must post that capital for every sock puppet, and any fake answer graders flag gets the whole stake slashed, not merely the reward withheld, so one detected thread of identities can burn far more than it hoped to farm. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count while expected yield stays flat.
